one_liner: Serde-compatible Rust JSON library using SIMD; about 1.7-2.8x faster than serde_json at typed parsing on x86_64.
what_it_does: A JSON library for Rust from CloudWeGo (the Volo team) that plugs into serde. sonic_rs::from_str, from_slice, to_string and to_vec work on any Serialize/Deserialize type, so typed code can often switch by changing the crate path. It also has its own mutable sonic_rs::Value DOM with a json! macro and pointer! paths, plus lazy APIs: get and get_many pull fields by path without a full parse, to_array_iter and to_object_iter iterate lazily, and LazyValue, OwnedLazyValue and RawNumber replace serde_json's RawValue and arbitrary-precision numbers.
how_it_is_fast: It does not use simdjson's two-stage structural-index/tape design. It is a single-pass recursive-descent parser that feeds serde visitors or the DOM directly, with no intermediate tape; the README credits this for beating simd-json on structs. SIMD (SSE2/AVX2 on x86_64, NEON on aarch64) speeds up the hot loops: string scanning with simdutf8 validation; whitespace skipping with simdjson's shuffle-table classifier and a cached 64-bit non-space bitmap; JSONSki-style bracket counting over a PCLMULQDQ prefix-XOR in-string mask, which skips whole containers for the get and lazy APIs; and a 32-byte copy-and-find escape loop on output. Numbers are parsed with 8-digit SWAR plus an Eisel-Lemire fast path and printed with zmij (Schubfach-based). The Value DOM uses a bumpalo arena, stores objects as flat key/value arrays instead of hash maps, and points strings into a padded copy of the input.
when_to_use: Rust services on x86_64 built with AVX2+PCLMULQDQ enabled that deserialize multi-KB-to-MB payloads into serde structs. In the README, validated from_slice beats serde_json::from_str by 1.7-2.3x and serde_json::from_slice by 2.2-2.8x on twitter/citm_catalog/canada.

Parsing into an untyped DOM that is mostly read, not heavily key-searched. sonic_rs::Value parses 3.4-5.2x faster than serde_json::from_str into serde_json::Value on the Xeon, and 2.8-3.3x faster on Apple M1 Pro.

Pulling a few fields out of large documents you already trust. get_unchecked read a twitter.json field in 76.8 us vs 363 us for gjson, and get, get_many and the lazy iterators avoid building a DOM at all.
Serializing string-heavy data. twitter.json to_string took 390 us vs 797 us for serde_json (Value) and 448 vs 740 us (struct), thanks to the SIMD escape scan.
when_not_to_use: Small messages. In issue #150 a user's small-payload struct benchmark showed no gain over serde_json, and the maintainer answered that the JSON was too small to benefit from SIMD.

Portable x86_64 binaries built for the default baseline. The SIMD paths are chosen at compile time (cfg target_feature avx2+pclmulqdq), and there is no runtime CPU dispatch (issue #14 is still open). Without -C target-cpu=native or the matching target features you get the scalar fallback. A native build may not run on older CPUs.

Parsing untrusted, possibly deeply nested input into sonic_rs::Value, or using checked get_many on it. parser.rs has no depth guard, and 100,000 nested brackets abort the process with a stack overflow instead of returning an error (open issues #239 and #232). Typed serde deserialization is capped at 255 levels.
Non-mainstream targets. 32-bit x86 (i686) fails to build (open issues #228 and #231). RISC-V and other architectures use a scalar fallback that the README says may be 'very slower'.

Float-heavy serialization, or struct parsing on aarch64. serde_json matched or slightly beat it on canada.json serialization on both test CPUs. On M1 Pro, simd-json was faster at struct parsing of twitter and citm, and sonic-rs was only 1.1-1.7x ahead of serde_json::from_str.

integration.dependencies: ahash, bumpalo, bytes, cfg-if, faststr, itoa, ref-cast, serde, simdutf8, thiserror, zmij, plus in-repo sonic-number and sonic-simd
integration.min_toolchain: Stable Rust, edition 2021. No rust-version is declared. The code calls pointer expose_provenance (stable since Rust 1.84), so 1.84+ is inferred. The optional avx512 feature needs Rust 1.89+ and the avx512f target feature.
integration.platforms: x86_64 (fast path needs compile-time AVX2 + PCLMULQDQ + SSE2) and aarch64 (NEON). wasm32 gets simd128 in the SIMD layer. Other targets use a scalar fallback, and i686 currently fails to build. CI covers Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS, Windows and wasm32-wasip1.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented in prose. Value has unsafe Send + Sync impls; a parsed DOM sits in an Arc-shared arena. DOM parsing uses a thread-local node buffer, so concurrent parsing on separate threads is fine.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: typed serde (de)serialization uses the same from_str/from_slice/to_string/to_vec/to_writer/json! entry points. But Value/Object has a different, trait-based API with O(n) object lookup and kept duplicate keys. RawValue maps to LazyValue. The error type differs. from_reader buffers the whole input. #[serde(flatten)] into maps of sonic_rs::Value fails (open issue #114).

gotchas: Object::get on a parsed Value is a linear scan (documented as O(n); issue #168 is open). Duplicate keys are all kept, and get returns the first. The migration guide flags duplicate-key handling as a difference from serde_json::Value.

The *_unchecked APIs are unsafe. from_slice_unchecked skips UTF-8 validation, and get_unchecked/to_object_iter_unchecked assume valid JSON ('may return unexpected result'). from_str already takes the same no-validation path internally, because &str is valid UTF-8. So the README's from_slice_unchecked timings are what from_str gets.

Release builds read SIMD vectors past the end of a string tail when the read stays within the same page (check_cross_page), and LLVM sanitizers flag this. Hence the sanitize feature, which the README says costs about 30% of serialize speed and should not be used in production.

A parsed Value keeps a padded copy of the whole input plus a bumpalo arena alive. Parsing reserves len/2+2 node slots, thread-local up to 3 MB and heap above that. Inputs of 4 GB or more are rejected.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: In Rust, pick it over simd-json for serde-struct parsing or a mutable DOM on x86_64. Its README shows it 1.3-2.0x faster there, and it parses from an immutable &[u8]/&str, while simd-json's serde entry point takes &mut [u8]. On Apple M1 Pro, simd-json ties or wins struct parsing. jiter's catalogued ~2x over serde_json comes from a different benchmark, and bytedance/sonic is the Go sibling built on the same ideas.
verified_claims_summary: The numbers are first-party Criterion runs from the README, unchanged since late 2023 when the crate was about v0.3; the rustc, serde_json and simd-json versions are not stated. They were run on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8260 with -C target-cpu=native, LTO and jemalloc. Validated sonic_rs::from_slice parsed twitter.json into structs in 0.83 ms vs 1.38 ms for serde_json::from_str and 2.29 ms for from_slice, and parsed canada.json into an untyped Value in 4.96 ms vs 16.6-17.0 ms for serde_json; serde_json was about 2% faster at canada serialization.
status_note: Actively maintained under Apache-2.0: 0.5.9 and 0.5.10 shipped 2026-09-11, and the crate has about 6.8M crates.io downloads. It is usable today on stable Rust, but deep-nesting stack overflows and the i686 build failure are still open.
